November Timely Tips

November is here, and there are still plenty of things you can do in your garden before winter settles in! From protecting plants and putting fallen leaves to work to getting a jump on holiday projects, here are my timely tips for the month. 🍂

November Garden To-Do List

  • Watch that frosty forecast. Review my tips for preparing for a frosty forecast and protect your tender plants before temperatures drop.
  • Dig up and store tender bulbs. If you haven’t already, dig up and store tender bulbs such as gladiolus, cannas, dahlias and caladiums that you want to save for replanting next spring.
  • Protect your young trees. If you have newly planted trees, wrap their trunks with protective tree wrap to help prevent damage from nibbling rabbits and winter sunscald. Remember to remove the wraps in spring. If deer are a problem in your area, consider installing a sturdy, 4- to 5-foot-tall wire cage around young trees to protect against browsing and antler rubbing. Secure the cage with stakes and leave plenty of room for the tree to grow.
  • Keep watering. Cooler temperatures don’t mean your plants have stopped needing water. Continue watering during dry spells, especially newly planted trees, shrubs and perennials, until the ground freezes. Adequate moisture going into winter helps plants get off to a healthy start next spring. Check out my complete guide to watering outdoor plants for more tips.
  • Give strawberries a winter blanket. Protect your strawberry plants against winter cold with 2–4 inches of loose mulch. Fallen leaves or straw work well for this purpose.
  • Put those fallen leaves to work! Blow leaves into your garden beds rather than bagging them up. They’ll provide extra winter protection and, as they break down, become natural, nutrient-rich mulch that improves your soil. One of my favorite cheap tricks! Need another reason to ease up on fall cleanup? Here’s your permission to be messy.
  • It’s not too late to plant! If the ground hasn’t frozen, finish planting spring-flowering bulbs and garlic. As our fall weather seems to stay warmer longer, I find myself planting garlic in November instead of October more often. If you can still get through the ground, plant! Check out my tips for growing glorious garlic.
  • Start a holiday porch pot tradition. Gather friends and family and create your own beautiful holiday porch pots! Trimming greenery from your own trees or those of a friend makes for a low-cost, one-of-a-kind display. Add some pine cones, interesting branches, a festive bow or a few lights, and you’ve got something special. Check out my Holiday Porch Pots guide for inspiration and instructions. This is a wonderful project to enjoy together year after year!
  • Get a jump on holiday gift shopping. Looking for something special for the gardeners in your life? I’ve gathered clever, practical and delightful ideas in my Unique Gifts for the Gardener guide. You’ll find everything from hardworking garden tools to cozy favorites and fun surprises. You might even discover a little something for yourself!
  • Give the gift of a good gardening read. As the weather turns colder, it’s the perfect time to curl up with a good gardening book and grow your knowledge. Check out some of my favorites in Favorite Gardening Reads. And don’t forget my own books, Cheap Tricks Gardening and my newest release, Brylee’s Big Adventure: One Little Caterpillar’s Incredible Journey! Personally signed copies are available when you order directly from Midwest Garden Gal. I’d love to sign one for you or someone special on your gift list!

November is a wonderful time to wrap up those last garden chores, get creative and start dreaming about what’s ahead. Even as the growing season winds down, there’s always something to enjoy in and around the garden.

Happy gardening!

Lisa Hinzman Howard

Lisa Hinzman Howard is the founder of Midwest Garden Gal, LLC, where she helps gardeners grow with confidence through practical, research-based education. Lisa is the author of Cheap Tricks Gardening and Brylee's Big Adventure: One Little Caterpillar’s Incredible Journey.
